messages:
jordana: quick question — i'm trying to capture model-selection intent in a single routing ruleset for multitenant routes. goal: honor explicit alias pins, enforce compatibility constraints, and have a clear fallback. any preferences on expression shape? :thinking:
kevin: i'd split into two phases: route matching (path/headers) then selection pipeline (pin -> alias -> compat filter -> cost sort -> fallback). keeps logic testable.
maya: if we keep it single doc i'd prefer declarative stages rather than nesting lots of if/then. makes the console UI map to the rule pieces.
sam: fwiw we have edge cases: legacy clients set x-model-version, which we should treat as a pin but only if compatible with requested sequence length / features. otherwise reject or rewrite header.
jordana: here's a rough example i've been prototyping: ```
match: path == "/v1/generate" && header("x-client-type") != "internal"
selection: 
  - explicit_pin: header("x-model-alias") || header("x-model-version")
  - compatibility_filter: require(features.delta_seq_len <= model.max_seq)
  - scoring: prefer(by: [latency_cost, accuracy_estimate])
  - fallback: alias("redwood-stable")
```
kevin: i like the idea but compatibility_filter needs to be expressive: some models support partial compat (quantized variants) — we need a compatibility matrix lookup, not just simple numeric checks. maybe `compatible(model, request_context) -> reason` so we can surface failure reasons in telemetry.
maya: can we also expose a `pin_ttl` and `pin_scope` (tenant vs route) so console rollouts can pin temporarily? e.g., canary pins for 1h scoped to route.
sam: +1 on telemetry reasons. also suggest an override header precedence table: 1) admin-pin, 2) tenant-pin, 3) client-header-pin, 4) route-default. avoid surprising admin overrides.
jordana: re: console UX, we probably want to render the chain visually: Pin -> Compat -> Score -> Fallback, and let users click each node to see the rule and last-applied decisions. ops-bot: note: rollout-notifier triggered for rule change by jordana at 1892102258
kevin: implementation note: runtime should short-circuit when an explicit pin resolves to a compatible model to avoid running scoring. only go to scoring when multiple compatible candidates remain.
maya: edge-case: when alias points to a model family (alias -> variants). we need a deterministic tie-breaker (prefer same-gen quantized to avoid regen). document it.
sam: do we want automated fallback that can pick a lower-cost but compatible model under load? that requires coupling routing policy to quota/latency telemetry. think it's worth it but make it opt-in.
jordana: thanks — i'll draft a ruleset JSON schema and a console mock that maps to stages. will post a PR with examples and telemetry key names. if anyone wants to pair on the schema lmk. :thumbsup:
